image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a motorcycle front wheel assembly featuring a dual-disc brake system. The image prominently displays two cross-drilled steel rotors with machined surfaces, mounted on a silver alloy wheel hub. A red telescopic fork leg is visible in the center, flanked by a black and blue brake caliper on the left and a gold-colored caliper on the right. Hydraulic lines and mounting bolts are clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct circular rotors are visible. Their diameter is significantly larger than their thickness, consistent with standard disk brake geometry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A black/blue caliper is mounted on the left rotor, and a gold caliper is on the right. Both straddle the outer edge of the rotors correctly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors are attached to a central carrier which is bolted to the wheel hub. Multiple hexagonal bolt heads are clearly visible securing the assembly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors appear to be floating or semi-floating designs with visible gaps between the braking surface and the carrier, typical of ventilated motorcycle discs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While partially obscured by the caliper housing, the interface where the pads contact the rotor is implied by the caliper position. No structural impossibility is observed here.
Black hydraulic hoses are visible entering the top of the caliper bodies, consistent with hydraulic actuation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both rotors feature a distinct pattern of cross-drilled holes across the braking surface, a common performance feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors appear clean and silver/chrome. There is no significant blueing or browning indicative of extreme heat cycling; they look new or well-maintained.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The calipers exhibit the texture and finish of cast metal (likely aluminum alloy given the color anodizing/painting).

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific mechanical components (rotor, caliper, hub) align with the 'disk brake' class definition and distinguish from similar mechanical parts.
To verify the spatial relationship between the overlapping rotors, the fork leg, and the wheel hub, ensuring no geometric melting or depth collapse.
To check for boundary bleeding between the complex caliper shape and the background/rotor, and ensure hydraulic lines are continuous tubes.
To assess the realism of the metallic reflections, machining marks, and drilled holes for any texture anomalies common in AI generation.

focus_areas: Integrity of cross-drilled holes (regularity and depth)
Connection points of hydraulic lines to calipers
Spatial separation between dual rotors and fork leg
Realism of metallic reflections and machining marks
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the symmetry and regularity of the drilled holes on the rotors. AI often distorts repeating patterns. Verify that the bolts securing the rotors to the hub have consistent hexagonal shapes and correct perspective foreshortening. Check if the hydraulic lines maintain consistent diameter and do not merge into the caliper body unnaturally.
